donald-trump: "I HATE TAYLOR SWIFT" and the media as enemy of the people

In a September 17, 2024 Badlands Media essay, [[erik-carlson|Erik Carlson]] argued that Trump's all-capitals Truth Social post "I HATE TAYLOR SWIFT!", published shortly before a second assassination attempt on his life, should not be read as an impulsive insult but as a deliberate act of misdirection.[n] Carlson's thesis was that everything Trump communicates has a purpose, and that what critics read as missteps repeatedly "explodes in the Deep State's faces" rather than backfiring on Trump.[n] On this reading, Trump was not attacking [[taylor-swift|Taylor Swift]] the person but the [[cabal|Cabal]] machinery that manufactured her and uses celebrity to steer young women toward what Carlson called unfulfilling lives.[n]

Carlson also credited Trump's popularization of the phrase "[[fake-news|fake news]]" with being the moment when large numbers of Americans first entertained the possibility that televised information was not the whole truth.[n] He attributed the two assassination attempts against Trump in two months not to controversial statements but to elite fear that Trump would dismantle the system, and closed by saying he would vote for "the man the Satanic Cabal desperately wants dead."[n]
taylor-swift:
In "The Media is the Enemy of the People" (September 17, 2024), [[erik-carlson|Erik Carlson]] described Swift as "an American intelligence agency creation" built to influence and, in his phrasing, brainwash young girls and effeminate men.[n] He predicted that many lifelong Swifties would reach middle age unmarried and childless, and argued that the contemporaneous cultural discourse about "childless cat ladies" was not coincidental.[n]

Carlson placed Swift in a lineage of manufactured acts, writing that "God created [[elvis-presley|Elvis Presley]]" while "[[mi6|MI6]]/[[central-intelligence-agency|CIA]] created [[the-beatles|the Beatles]] and [[the-rolling-stones|Rolling Stones]]," and calling Swift "Gen Z's Beatles" — not musically comparable, but created in a similar fashion, for similar reasons, by similar people.[n] He asked whether genres such as pop and hip hop, and artists like Swift and [[beyonce|Beyonce]], were being actively promoted while rock was left "to rot on the vine."[n]
erik-carlson: "The Media is the Enemy of the People" (September 17, 2024)

Carlson's September 17, 2024 essay, subtitled "Most Media Companies Aren't Actual Businesses," argues that the American media system is not a commercial industry but an instrument of population control funded by the [[central-intelligence-agency|CIA]] and the money-printing capacity of the [[federal-reserve|Federal Reserve]].[n] He traces the model to the Roman formula of "[[bread-and-circuses|bread and circuses]]" coined by the poet Juvenal, updated by the psychological techniques of [[sigmund-freud|Sigmund Freud]], [[carl-jung|Carl Jung]] and [[edward-bernays|Edward Bernays]].[n]

The essay's central economic claim is that outlets such as [[cnn|CNN]], [[msnbc|MSNBC]] and [[fox-news|Fox News]] survive collapsing ratings because they are subsidized rather than sold, and that much advertising — particularly [[big-pharma|Big Pharma]]'s roughly 75% share of broadcast TV ad revenue — functions as both leverage over coverage and as [[advertising-as-money-laundering|money laundering]].[n] Carlson extends the argument to [[google|Google]], [[facebook|Facebook]], [[youtube|YouTube]] and modern art, and reads the advertiser exodus after [[elon-musk|Elon Musk]]'s purchase of [[twitter|Twitter]] as the withdrawal of CIA-directed money.[n] He frames Trump's "I HATE TAYLOR SWIFT" post as an attack on the system that manufactures celebrities rather than on [[taylor-swift|Taylor Swift]] herself.[n] Badlands Media notes that its articles represent the opinions of contributing authors.[n]
central-intelligence-agency: Alleged control of media, technology and culture (Carlson, 2024)

In "The Media is the Enemy of the People" (September 17, 2024), [[erik-carlson|Erik Carlson]] argued that the CIA, formed in the latter half of 1947, moved to capture American mass media as television penetration rose from 9% to 65% of homes during the 1950s, with [[operation-mockingbird|Operation Mockingbird]] believed to have begun by the early 1960s.[n] Carlson wrote that music, movies, television news and entertainment, newspapers and magazines were funded, created and manipulated by the agency, so that the body created to defend America from foreign enemies was in fact controlling Americans.[n]

He further claimed the CIA created 1960s counterculture and music groups, was heavily involved in the civil rights and women's rights movements, and "created serial killers and political assassins," removing opponents by assassination or character assassination.[n] With the arrival of the public internet the agency allegedly pivoted, creating [[google|Google]] and [[facebook|Facebook]] to control what could be found and said online while harvesting personal data, and letting print outlets die as funding shifted.[n] Carlson also described the CIA as "the biggest gun running, drug running and human trafficking operation in the world," whose proceeds require laundering through advertising, modern art and [[youtube|YouTube]] earnings.[n]
cia: [[erik-carlson|Erik Carlson]]'s September 17, 2024 essay "The Media is the Enemy of the People" presents the CIA as the operational center of American media manipulation, from [[operation-mockingbird|Operation Mockingbird]] in the early 1960s through the funding of [[google|Google]] and [[facebook|Facebook]] in the internet era.[n] Carlson argues the agency is indifferent to the medium — broadcast, print or online — so long as manipulation and preoccupation continue.[n]
federal-reserve: [[erik-carlson|Erik Carlson]]'s September 17, 2024 essay argues that the creation of the Federal Reserve in 1913 gave the [[cabal|Cabal]] the ability to print money "out of nothing, backed by nothing," supplying the unlimited funding required for a mass propaganda apparatus, with the cost passed to the public through inflation — in his words "the greatest scam of all time."[n] He notes that [[hollywood|Hollywood]] and national radio took off at the same moment the Fed was created, and calls the sequence no coincidence.[n]
operation-mockingbird: In "The Media is the Enemy of the People" (September 17, 2024), [[erik-carlson|Erik Carlson]] dated the believed start of Operation Mockingbird to the early 1960s, when the majority of American homes had acquired a television, and described it as a covert operation in which the [[central-intelligence-agency|CIA]] funded members of the media to push messaging the agency wanted the public to consume.[n] He placed its launch shortly after the CIA's formation in 1947 and treated it as the template for decades of narrative control.[n]
edward-bernays: [[erik-carlson|Erik Carlson]]'s September 17, 2024 Badlands Media essay names Bernays — nephew of [[sigmund-freud|Sigmund Freud]] — alongside Freud and [[carl-jung|Carl Jung]] as the figures who "developed and perfected" techniques capable not merely of keeping people from thinking but of changing how they think, supplying the psychological toolkit that modernized the Roman formula of [[bread-and-circuses|bread and circuses]].[n]
sigmund-freud: In "The Media is the Enemy of the People" (September 17, 2024), [[erik-carlson|Erik Carlson]] grouped Freud with [[carl-jung|Carl Jung]] and his nephew [[edward-bernays|Edward Bernays]] as developers of the mind-manipulation techniques later deployed through mass media.[n]
carl-jung: [[erik-carlson|Erik Carlson]]'s September 17, 2024 essay lists Jung with [[sigmund-freud|Sigmund Freud]] and [[edward-bernays|Edward Bernays]] as architects of techniques for changing how populations think, which Carlson argues were operationalized once the [[federal-reserve|Federal Reserve]] and later the [[central-intelligence-agency|CIA]] provided funding and distribution.[n]
elon-musk: [[erik-carlson|Erik Carlson]]'s September 17, 2024 essay cites Musk's purchase of [[twitter|Twitter]] and the roughly 60% loss of advertising that followed as evidence for its central claim.[n] Carlson asks whether advertisers left of their own accord or whether the [[central-intelligence-agency|CIA]] simply stopped funding the platform through companies it controls, noting that the money dried up at the same time the [[fbi|FBI]] and CIA were pushed out of the company.[n]
google: [[erik-carlson|Erik Carlson]]'s September 17, 2024 essay claims Google exists because the [[central-intelligence-agency|CIA]] created its technology and funds it, with its purpose being to control what is found online while collecting personal information for the agency.[n] Carlson questions how a search engine earns money from users at all, comparing it to Starbucks profiting from someone who uses its Wi-Fi and bathroom without buying anything, and argues advertising provides cover for revenues that actually originate with the CIA.[n]
facebook: In "The Media is the Enemy of the People" (September 17, 2024), [[erik-carlson|Erik Carlson]] wrote that Facebook, like [[google|Google]], was created and funded by the [[central-intelligence-agency|CIA]] as a response to the loss of narrative control caused by the public internet, tasked with policing what is said online and passing user data to the agency.[n] He described social media advertising revenue as "a farce" masking government money.[n]
twitter: Advertising collapse after the Musk purchase (Carlson, 2024)

[[erik-carlson|Erik Carlson]]'s September 17, 2024 essay recounts that [[elon-musk|Elon Musk]] lost roughly 60% of Twitter's advertising immediately after buying the platform, and that subsequent disclosures showed how involved the [[fbi|FBI]] and [[central-intelligence-agency|CIA]] had been in controlling speech, shadow banning users and removing others.[n] Carlson treats the coincidence of the agencies' expulsion and the advertising collapse as support for his claim that advertising functions as a CIA laundering and control mechanism.[n]
hollywood: [[erik-carlson|Erik Carlson]]'s September 17, 2024 essay argues that Hollywood was built in Southern California only after the [[federal-reserve|Federal Reserve]] created an endless supply of free money, and that the pairing was not coincidental.[n] Writing in 2024, he predicted the year would be among the worst ever for movie ticket sales without the excuse of the 2020 theater shutdowns, blaming "woke" product and asserting that Hollywood "isn't allowed to make the movies people want to see."[n] He contrasted a summer with one or two blockbusters against earlier eras when one or two arrived weekly, and asked how theaters remain in business at all.[n]
mi6: Alleged role in manufacturing British rock acts (Carlson, 2024)

[[erik-carlson|Erik Carlson]]'s September 17, 2024 Badlands Media essay asserts that "God created [[elvis-presley|Elvis Presley]]" while "the MI6/[[central-intelligence-agency|CIA]] created [[the-beatles|the Beatles]] and [[the-rolling-stones|Rolling Stones]]," framing the British bands as imitations engineered for cultural influence rather than organic phenomena.[n]
hunter-biden: Cited in the modern-art money-laundering argument (Carlson, 2024)

[[erik-carlson|Erik Carlson]]'s September 17, 2024 essay invokes Biden's painting career as an illustration of the claim that the [[central-intelligence-agency|CIA]] created modern art as a laundering vehicle, stating flatly that "Hunter Biden is not an artistic genius" and that a banana duct-taped to a wall is not worth millions.[n] Carlson's general rule is that any market where value is purely subjective makes a good laundering tool.[n]
fbi: [[erik-carlson|Erik Carlson]]'s September 17, 2024 essay states that disclosures after [[elon-musk|Elon Musk]]'s purchase of [[twitter|Twitter]] revealed how involved the FBI and [[central-intelligence-agency|CIA]] were inside the company, controlling permissible speech, shadow banning some users and removing others outright.[n] Carlson links their expulsion to the platform's sudden loss of advertising.[n]
cnn: Cited as a non-business media outlet (Carlson, 2024)

[[erik-carlson|Erik Carlson]]'s September 17, 2024 essay names CNN, alongside [[msnbc|MSNBC]] and [[fox-news|Fox News]], as proof that media companies are not real businesses: ratings plummet, audiences reject the product, and yet the outlets continue operating and pushing the same messaging — behavior he says would bankrupt any firm not underwritten by government money.[n]
msnbc: Cited as a non-business media outlet (Carlson, 2024)

In "The Media is the Enemy of the People" (September 17, 2024), [[erik-carlson|Erik Carlson]] cited MSNBC with [[cnn|CNN]] and [[fox-news|Fox News]] as networks whose survival despite collapsing ratings demonstrates that they are instruments of manipulation rather than commercial enterprises.[n]
fox-news: Cited as a non-business media outlet (Carlson, 2024)

[[erik-carlson|Erik Carlson]]'s September 17, 2024 essay pointedly includes Fox News — "and even FOX News" — among the outlets that keep broadcasting what he calls disinformation while their ratings fall, which he offers as evidence of external subsidy rather than market discipline.[n]
youtube: [[erik-carlson|Erik Carlson]]'s September 17, 2024 essay asks how YouTube stars are able to earn so much money, and answers that the platform serves both to preoccupy audiences and to launder [[central-intelligence-agency|CIA]] money.[n]
beyonce: [[erik-carlson|Erik Carlson]]'s September 17, 2024 essay names Beyonce with [[taylor-swift|Taylor Swift]] when asking whether pop and hip hop are genres actively pushed by the [[central-intelligence-agency|CIA]] while rock has been "left to rot on the vine."[n]
big-pharma: [[erik-carlson|Erik Carlson]]'s September 17, 2024 Badlands Media essay states that 75% of broadcast television advertising revenue comes from Big Pharma, and argues the spending is not needed to sell drugs — given the industry's grip on government and the medical community — but to control what the media says about it, making the industry "the media's biggest sugar daddy."[n]
cabal: Bread and circuses in the modern era (Carlson, 2024)

[[erik-carlson|Erik Carlson]]'s September 17, 2024 essay describes the Cabal as still using the Roman tactic of [[bread-and-circuses|bread and circuses]]: welfare, food stamps and financial assistance calibrated to keep the poor dependent and quiescent, while the working and middle classes are absorbed by television, movies, video games, music and sports.[n] Carlson adds that modern distraction extends into manipulation and mind control, and observes that polling shows elites consume far less media than lower- and middle-income Americans.[n] He concludes that unless a reader is over a hundred years old, their entire life has been lived under Cabal media manipulation, and that Trump's hatred of [[taylor-swift|Taylor Swift]] is really hatred of "the Cabal who runs the world."[n]
deep-state: [[erik-carlson|Erik Carlson]]'s September 17, 2024 essay argues that Trump's apparent missteps consistently "explode in the Deep State's faces," and that the two attempts on his life within two months were driven not by controversial statements but by fear that he would bring down the system.[n]
fake-news: [[erik-carlson|Erik Carlson]]'s September 17, 2024 essay credits Trump's use of the phrase "fake news" with being the point at which most Americans first considered that what they saw on television might not be the truth, calling it a stark realization to accept lifelong manipulation.[n]
ruby-ridge: [[erik-carlson|Erik Carlson]]'s September 17, 2024 essay lists Ruby Ridge with [[waco-siege|Waco]] and the [[oklahoma-city-bombing|Oklahoma City Bombing]] as events he says were not coincidentally clustered in the early-to-mid 1990s, when the internet went public and citizens began challenging the government — serving, in his reading, to make examples of dissenters and to paint anti-government groups as crazy, hateful and violent.[n]
waco-siege: In "The Media is the Enemy of the People" (September 17, 2024), [[erik-carlson|Erik Carlson]] grouped Waco with [[ruby-ridge|Ruby Ridge]] and the [[oklahoma-city-bombing|Oklahoma City Bombing]] as a coordinated response to the loss of narrative control that accompanied the public internet.[n]
oklahoma-city-bombing: [[erik-carlson|Erik Carlson]]'s September 17, 2024 essay places the mid-1990s Oklahoma City Bombing alongside [[ruby-ridge|Ruby Ridge]] and [[waco-siege|Waco]] as part of a pattern he says was designed to discredit and deter anti-government sentiment just as the internet went public.[n]
money-laundering: Advertising and modern art as laundering vehicles (Carlson, 2024)

[[erik-carlson|Erik Carlson]]'s September 17, 2024 Badlands Media essay argues that advertising is an ideal laundering mechanism because its effect on sales cannot be quantified, making billions in spending impossible to audit.[n] He applies the same logic to modern art — where value is purely subjective — and to social media and [[youtube|YouTube]] revenues, comparing the arrangement to the car wash used to launder Walter White's methamphetamine proceeds on *Breaking Bad*.[n] The funds requiring laundering, in his account, are money created out of nothing by the [[federal-reserve|Federal Reserve]] together with the proceeds of gun running, drug running and human trafficking he attributes to the [[central-intelligence-agency|CIA]].[n]
truth-social: Trump's all-capitals post "I HATE TAYLOR SWIFT!" on Truth Social, published shortly before the second assassination attempt against him in 2024, became the framing device for [[erik-carlson|Erik Carlson]]'s September 17, 2024 Badlands Media essay on media control.[n] Carlson read the post as deliberate misdirection aimed at the system behind [[taylor-swift|Taylor Swift]] rather than at the singer.[n]
